national.title: How to Renew Your Driving Licence Online in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to renewing an expiring or expired driving licence on the Sarathi Parivahan portal. Verified statutory fees of ₹400, medical Form 1A rules, and late penalty exemptions.

steps.title: Open Sarathi Parivahan and Choose Your State
steps.description: Visit sarathi.parivahan.gov.in and select the state where you currently reside.
steps.calloutText: You can apply for renewal up to one year before your driving licence expires without penalty.

steps.title: Select 'Apply for DL Renewal' from Services
steps.description: Click 'Services on Driving Licence' and choose 'Apply for DL Renewal' from the list of services.

steps.title: Enter Driving Licence Number and Date of Birth
steps.description: Type your current driving licence number and date of birth to fetch your licence records from the national database.
steps.calloutText: Enter your DL number with exact spaces and state code as printed on your plastic card.

steps.title: Confirm Address Details and Select Renewal
steps.description: Verify your personal details. If your address has changed, check 'Change of Address' to update your records simultaneously.

steps.title: Upload Form 1A Medical Certificate and Old DL
steps.description: Upload a scanned copy of your old driving licence. If aged 40 or above, upload Form 1A signed by a registered doctor.
steps.calloutText: Form 1A must contain the doctor's state medical council registration number and official rubber stamp.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Government Renewal Fee Online
steps.description: Pay ₹200 for renewal and ₹200 for smart card printing. Pay via net banking, debit card, or UPI.

steps.title: Submit via Aadhaar e-KYC for Faceless Processing
steps.description: Authenticate using Aadhaar OTP to complete paperless submission. No physical visit to the RTO is required in contactless states.

steps.title: Receive Renewed Smart Card DL via Speed Post
steps.description: Once approved, your renewed driving licence card is printed and sent via Speed Post. Digital DL updates on DigiLocker immediately.
steps.where: Delivered to Residence & Available on DigiLocker

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Form 1A Medical Certificate for Applicants Aged 40+
rejectionReasons.description: Applicants aged 40 or older who submit without a registered doctor signed Form 1A will have their application halted.
rejectionReasons.solution: Get Form 1A signed by a registered MBBS doctor with their registration seal before uploading.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying with DL Expired Over 1 Year Without Late Fees
rejectionReasons.description: Under Section 15 of the Motor Vehicles Act, late renewal attracts a statutory penalty of ₹300 per year.
rejectionReasons.solution: Pay the calculated late fee on the Sarathi portal to avoid rejection by the scrutiny clerk.

rejectionReasons.title: Legacy DL Records Not Found in National Sarathi Database
rejectionReasons.description: Very old manual book licences issued before digitization may not appear automatically on Sarathi.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for 'DL Backlog Entry' first at your issuing RTO with your physical booklet.

rejectionReasons.title: Submitting Incomplete Proof for Address Change
rejectionReasons.description: Requesting an address change without uploading a matching Aadhaar card or electricity bill causes delay.
rejectionReasons.solution: Upload a clear government document displaying your exact current residential address.

rejectionReasons.title: Blurry Scan of Existing Driving Licence
rejectionReasons.description: Uploading a cropped or unreadable photo of the old licence prevents document verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Scan both front and back sides of the plastic card cleanly in PDF format under 200 KB.

rejectionReasons.title: Pending Traffic E-Challans or Suspension Orders
rejectionReasons.description: An active court suspension or unpaid traffic challan linked to the licence blocks the renewal workflow.
rejectionReasons.solution: Clear all pending e-challans on the echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal before applying for renewal.

faqItems.question: When can I apply to renew my driving licence in India?
faqItems.answer: You can apply up to one year before your licence expires and within one year after expiry without penalty.

faqItems.question: Is a medical certificate compulsory for driving licence renewal?
faqItems.answer: It is compulsory for applicants aged 40 or above and for commercial transport licence holders.

faqItems.question: What is the fee for renewing a driving licence before expiry?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹200 for licence renewal plus ₹200 for smart card printing, totaling ₹400.

faqItems.question: What is the penalty for renewing a driving licence after one year of expiry?
faqItems.answer: A late penalty of ₹300 per additional year or part of year applies under the amended Motor Vehicles Act.

faqItems.question: Can I renew my driving licence online without visiting the RTO?
faqItems.answer: Yes. States offering Aadhaar e-KYC provide contactless online renewal without any physical RTO visit.

faqItems.question: What happens if my driving licence has been expired for more than 5 years?
faqItems.answer: You must pay the penalty and re-appear for the practical driving test before your licence is renewed.

faqItems.question: Can I change my residential address during DL renewal?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Select 'Change of Address' in DL services and upload proof of your new residential address.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to receive the renewed smart card DL?
faqItems.answer: It typically arrives within 7 to 15 days via Speed Post. The digital licence updates on DigiLocker immediately.
